impl.summary:
Implemented the 10-node caterpillar (cat10) that adds the MISSING depth-0/root top-2 sibling, flag-gated behind FR13_CAT10_ROOT_SIBLING (default OFF = byte-identical to cat9). CPU-only, no GPU boot.

Root cause confirmed in source: cat9 had top-2 leaves at depths 1-4 but NONE at depth 0 — the drafter computes the root argmax only and the comment at line 9620-9621 explicitly states the root runner-up is unused. That is the structural reason 62% of greedy rejects are at step-0/d0 with no root-branch rescue.

The codebase is overwhelmingly topology-driven: parent/ancestry/visible masks, both committers (greedy LCP + temp>0 sampling), eager-pack replay rows, and conv-fusion prior windows ALL derive from the SPEC_CONFIG tree_choices and auto-adapt to 10 nodes. The ONLY hand-rolled 9-node code is the drafter's caterpillar packing — so all correctness edits are concentrated in propose_tree (engagement flag, capture root rank-2 token from the existing root logits with no extra lm-head read, new 10-element pack order matching vLLM's (len,path) sort where (1,) lands at node id 2). cat10's n_pad stays 16 and max path depth stays 6 (sibling is depth-1, doesn't deepen the tree), so NO new state-cache/h_cache spill vs cat9 — the only speed cost is +1 lm-head verify row.

Validated: patch + launcher syntax clean; embedded propose_tree body AST-compiles; OFF-path boolean equivalence proved by enumeration; cat10 parent/ancestry derivation confirmed (node2=(1,) parent=root, ancestry={root}); every depth 0-4 now carries top-1 spine + top-2 sibling. Did NOT boot/run (CPU-only task) and did NOT git commit (monitor commits).

gate.summary: Ran the full B=1 cat10 gate, serialized one container at a time (recover_host_memory clean between each boot, all full-health). Three axes vs cat9 control and native E5, lossless ref = the no-spec recurrent oracle. RESULT: cat10 is NOT a net win. (1) LOSSLESS flat: 22 clear-margin flips vs oracle, identical to cat9's 22 (cat9 reproduced the banked baseline exactly, validating the oracle); the root sibling redistributed flips (p0 6->2, p2 4->8) but total unchanged, per-position rate marginally higher (4.81% vs 4.56%). (2) ACCEPT: the d0 rescue is REAL but small (d0 rate 0.871->0.906, +0.0353) yet total accept/event DROPPED 3.198->2.932 because the extra root-sibling verify row dilutes acceptance at every deeper spine position (d1-d4 all fell). (3) SPEED: +1 verify row costs 1.013x s/fwd and net TPS regressed (18.40->17.08 warm, 16.01->15.17 per-req median) with no accept gain to offset. The d0-rescue hypothesis partially validated at d0 but the downstream dilution more than cancels it. Recommend keeping cat9 default, cat10 flag OFF. Artifacts in output/fr13_cat10/ (cat9|cat10|native_e5|oracle subdirs: accept_speed.json, capture.json, flips_vs_oracle.json, metrics_final.txt); draft bind /home/mark/shared/lumoFlyWheel/FR13_CAT10_BIND.md (no commit). CAVEAT: whole-window accept/event and native_e5's absolute number are trajectory-confounded draws (different greedy streams, served_lens differ; native p2/p3 EOS'd early this boot) — the binding facts are the 22-vs-22 flip equality and the +0.0353 d0 rate delta with the -0.27 total accept drop.

cat10Verify.recommendation: Keep cat9 as default; cat10 flag (FR13_CAT10_ROOT_SIBLING) stays OFF. Do NOT ship cat10. Next move: pursue the DRIFT-FIX FIRST (the conv prior-window / committer non-argmax deep-row defect — the ~22 clear-margin flips and the d1-d4 dilution are the real ceiling), then revisit topology. The root-sibling approach is the wrong lever: the d0 reject problem is real but a brute extra verify row dilutes the spine more than it rescues d0. A better future lever per the tree-reshape memory is a SHALLOWER tree (reduce depth-accumulation) or making the root sibling REPLACE a deep low-yield row (d4 only accepts 32-38%) rather than ADD to the row count — so net verify rows stay flat. Re-run the gate only after the committer drift is fixed, since the lossless floor (22 flips, worse-severity in cat10) is the binding blocker, not topology.
cat10Verify.issues:
VERDICT HOLDS: cat10 = no_help is correct and the binding facts reproduce exactly from raw artifacts. All four axes verified, with two material caveats the summary under-weights.

VERIFIED CLEAN:
- ENGAGEMENT (PASS, robust): cat10 draft_tokens/drafts = 5850/585 = exactly 10.0; cat9 = 9.0; native_e5 = 5.0 (depth-matched, drafts==5 confirmed). Oracle has ZERO spec_decode counters in metrics_final.txt = genuine no-spec boot (speculative_config=None), NOT a prefill/spec arm; the three spec arms have 40/42/32 counters. FA2 fork sha256 byte-identical (97fa25...) between cat9 and cat10 = same binary. Within-boot determinism 4/4 True on all 4 live arms (class-8 first gate cleared). CAVEAT: the textual drafter engagement line cited in the bind ("FR13_CAT10_ROOT_SIBLING drafter topology: cat10=True (env=1)...") is NOT persisted in any output/fr13_cat10/ artifact — launch.log is only 4 lines (mem-recovery preamble), and fr10_caterpillar_drafter.jsonl was not saved. Engagement is proven only via the metrics draft-toks/event=10.0, which is sufficient and non-vacuous (a silent-cat9 boot would read 9.0), but the human-readable proof line is unverifiable from the saved files.
- ACCEPT (decisive): d0 rescue REAL at raw-count level — cat9 d0 101/116=0.8707 vs cat10 106/117=0.9060 (+5 accepts, +0.0353). With near-identical draft volume (116 vs 117 forwards), the comparison is apples-to-apples: cat10 LOSES 33 accepts at d1-d4 (d1 -0.101 rate, -11 count; d2 -8; d3 -7; d4 -7), net -28 accepts, accept/event 3.198->2.932. The d1 drop (-0.101) is far beyond trajectory noise -> dilution is MECHANISTIC. Native depth-match confirmed (num_spec=5, drafts==5).
- SPEED (honest): s/fwd 0.2258->0.2287 = +1.3% (the predicted +1 lm-head verify row; ~2.9 ms/fwd at B=1, not the 15 ms/row upper bound). Net TPS regressed: warm 18.40->17.08, per-req median 16.01->15.17; every per-request TPS dropped. Not amortized because accept/event fell. Mechanically sound.

TWO MATERIAL CAVEATS (do not overturn the verdict, but the bind under-states them):
1. LOSSLESS "flat" is true ONLY on COUNT (22==22). The flip SETS are at entirely different positions (cat9 and cat10 walk different greedy trajectories), and cat10's flips are SUBSTANTIALLY WORSE in magnitude: sum-deviation 84.8->132.2 nat, mean 3.86->6.01, max 9.4->17.25 nat, and 4 flips exceed 10 nat in cat10 vs ZERO in cat9. The flips are distributed throughout (not a single post-divergence cascade), so they are independent committer non-argmax defects. "Lossless flat / not regressed" should read "flip COUNT flat; per-flip SEVERITY regressed; neither arm is clean-lossless (~22 committer defects persist)."
2. TRAJECTORY CONFOUND is correctly flagged for whole-window accept/native_e5, but the per-depth RATE comparison (the bind's claimed "fair read") is ALSO mildly trajectory-confounded since cat9/cat10 produce different streams (served_lens [98,128,128,128] vs [73,128,128,128]). The decisive, confound-resistant read is the per-depth raw COUNT decomposition at matched draft volume (+5 d0 / -33 deep / -28 net), which I recomputed and which fully supports the verdict.

VERDICT FOLLOWS MECHANICALLY: not accept_win_speed_cost (accept FELL, so there is no win to trade against the +1-row cost). cat10 loses on accept (net -28), loses on speed (TPS down), flat-to-worse on lossless. no_help is correct.
